::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Sept 11th [1886]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection
:::

My dear [Miss Dampier](people/person_404.qmd)

So many thanks from [Gertrude](people/person_1462.qmd) doubly!

You will like to hear that [Philip](people/person_235.qmd) and [Margaret Buston](people/person_234.qmd) walked over here yesterday with some Grapes for Gertrude.[^1] They gave a very good account of their [mother](people/person_236.qmd). There is no house to be had at Twyford, so they are looking for one at Winchester which is wiser, I do not think settling in one’s former parish is ever advisable 

Poor [Mrs Monroe](people/person_1033.qmd) does not find it so. What a beautiful garden she has made.

There will be no college meeting till October so nothing can be done about the living before that

With Gertrude’s love
Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Philip and Margaret Buston were two of the numerous children of the Rev. [Roger Buston](people/person_233.qmd) (1807-September 1886), Vicar of Twyford.  Evidently this letter is written shortly after his death, when his widow and children were looking for a new home.
